summary.text: Sharice Davids is the Democratic incumbent representing Kansas's 3rd District, first elected in 2018 and in office since January 2019. A member of the Ho-Chunk Nation, she is a Cornell-trained lawyer who worked in economic development on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation, was a White House Fellow, and competed professionally in mixed martial arts before entering politics. She is seeking a fifth term.

paragraphs.text: According to her official House biography, she was raised by a single mother who served in the Army for 20 years, graduated from Leavenworth High School, and was a first-generation college student who worked throughout college.

Earned an associate degree from Johnson County Community College (2003), a bachelor's degree in business administration from the University of Missouri-Kansas City (2007), and a law degree from Cornell Law School (2010).

Worked as an associate at SNR Denton and as of-counsel at Ceiba Legal, as chair of the board of Twelve Clans, Inc. for the Ho-Chunk Nation, as deputy director of the Thunder Valley Community Development Corporation on the Pine Ridge Indian Reservation, and as director of economic development at Red Cloud Indian School.
Served as a White House Fellow in the Department of Transportation under President Barack Obama.
Is a member of the Ho-Chunk Nation and competed in professional mixed martial arts (1-1 record).
Elected to the U.S. House in 2018, succeeding Kevin Yoder, and took office January 3, 2019; she and Deb Haaland of New Mexico were among the first two Native American women elected to Congress.
In the 2025-2026 Congress she serves on the House Agriculture Committee and the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee.
Her official biography lists her residence as Roeland Park.
